s.t: Gulliver was a man from England.
s.fr: Gulliver était un homme d’Angleterre.

s.t: He went to sea on great ships, for he wanted to see far lands.
s.fr: Il alla en mer sur de grands navires, car il voulait voir des terres lointaines.

s.t: His ship sailed for many days over the wide sea.
s.fr: Son navire navigua pendant de nombreux jours sur la vaste mer.

s.t: A storm came in the night, and the wind drove the ship through the dark.
s.fr: Une tempête arriva dans la nuit, et le vent poussa le navire dans l’obscurité.

paras.summary: Gulliver, a man from England who wants to see far lands, sails for many days until a storm catches the ship in the night.

s.t: Waves came over the ship, and the masts fell.
s.fr: Des vagues passèrent sur le navire, et les mâts tombèrent.

s.t: The ship hit rocks, and the sea came in.
s.fr: Le navire heurta des rochers, et la mer entra.

s.t: The men could not hold the ship on the water.
s.fr: Les hommes ne pouvaient pas tenir le navire sur l’eau.

s.t: Gulliver and 6 of the men got away in a small boat.
s.fr: Gulliver et 6 des hommes s’échappèrent dans un petit bateau.

s.t: But a great wave threw the boat over in the dark.
s.fr: Mais une grande vague renversa le bateau dans l’obscurité.

s.t: The boat and the other men were gone.
s.fr: Le bateau et les autres hommes avaient disparu.

paras.summary: The storm breaks the masts and drives the ship onto rocks; the men cannot hold the ship, and Gulliver and six others escape in a small boat, but a wave throws it over and the other men are lost.

s.t: Gulliver could not see the land, but he swam on through the waves.
s.fr: Gulliver ne voyait pas la terre, mais il nagea à travers les vagues.

s.t: He swam and swam, and his arms grew weak.
s.fr: Il nagea et nagea, et ses bras devinrent faibles.

s.t: His feet found ground under the water.
s.fr: Ses pieds trouvèrent le sol sous l’eau.

s.t: He walked through the shallow sea to a dark shore.
s.fr: Il traversa la mer peu profonde jusqu’à une rive sombre.

s.t: He saw no houses and no fire on the shore.
s.fr: Il ne vit ni maisons ni feu sur la rive.

paras.summary: Gulliver swims on without seeing land until his arms grow weak, finds ground under his feet, and walks through shallow water to a dark shore with no houses and no fire.

s.t: The grass under his feet was soft.
s.fr: L’herbe sous ses pieds était douce.

s.t: He lay down on the grass and slept.
s.fr: Il s’allongea sur l’herbe et dormit.

paras.summary: Too tired to look around, he lies down on the soft grass and sleeps all night, alone on a strange shore.

s.t: Day came, and Gulliver woke.
s.fr: Le jour vint, et Gulliver se réveilla.

s.t: He lay on the grass, but he could not move.
s.fr: Il était allongé sur l’herbe, mais il ne pouvait pas bouger.

s.t: His arms, his legs, and his head were tied down.
s.fr: Ses bras, ses jambes et sa tête étaient attachés au sol.

s.t: More than 600 thin threads held him to the ground.
s.fr: Plus de 600 fils fins le retenaient au sol.

paras.summary: Gulliver wakes on the grass and finds he cannot move: his arms, legs, and head are tied down by hundreds of thin threads.

s.t: Small feet walked up his leg.
s.fr: De petits pieds montèrent le long de sa jambe.

s.t: They came up over his chest, man after man.
s.fr: Ils montèrent sur sa poitrine, homme après homme.

s.t: Gulliver looked down and saw a man no taller than his hand.
s.fr: Gulliver regarda en bas et vit un homme pas plus grand que sa main.

s.t: The little man pointed an arrow at Gulliver's face.
s.fr: Le petit homme pointa une flèche vers le visage de Gulliver.

s.t: 40 more little men came up and walked over him, from legs to head.
s.fr: 40 autres petits hommes montèrent et marchèrent sur lui, des jambes à la tête.

paras.summary: Small feet walk up his leg and over his chest, and Gulliver sees a man no taller than his hand pointing an arrow at his face, while forty more little men walk over him.

s.t: The men ran down to the ground when Gulliver shouted.
s.fr: Les hommes coururent vers le sol quand Gulliver cria.

s.t: Gulliver pulled, and one arm came free of the threads.
s.fr: Gulliver tira, et un bras se libéra des fils.

s.t: 100 arrows, small as needles, came down on his hand.
s.fr: 100 flèches, petites comme des aiguilles, tombèrent sur sa main.

s.t: The little arrows hurt, but they could not go deep.
s.fr: Les petites flèches faisaient mal, mais elles ne pouvaient pas aller loin.

s.t: When Gulliver moved his arm, more arrows came down.
s.fr: Quand Gulliver bougea son bras, d’autres flèches tombèrent.

s.t: He lay still on the grass and waited.
s.fr: Il resta immobile sur l’herbe et attendit.

paras.summary: The men run down when Gulliver shouts; he pulls one arm free, but arrows small as needles come down on his hand, so he lies still and waits.

s.t: A lord of the little men climbed up on Gulliver's chest and spoke.
s.fr: Un seigneur des petits hommes monta sur la poitrine de Gulliver et parla.

s.t: Gulliver could not understand the words.
s.fr: Gulliver ne pouvait pas comprendre les mots.

s.t: Gulliver put one free hand to his mouth to show he wanted food.
s.fr: Gulliver porta une main libre à sa bouche pour montrer qu’il voulait de la nourriture.

s.t: The little people understood, and they were not afraid of the giant.
s.fr: Les petites gens comprirent, et ils n’avaient pas peur du géant.

paras.summary: To the little men Gulliver is a giant; a lord climbs up and speaks words Gulliver cannot understand, and when Gulliver signs that he is hungry, the people are no longer afraid.

s.t: Soon the little people brought food to the giant.
s.fr: Bientôt les petites gens apportèrent de la nourriture au géant.

s.t: 100 men carried meat and bread up to Gulliver's mouth.
s.fr: 100 hommes portèrent de la viande et du pain jusqu’à la bouche de Gulliver.

s.t: Gulliver ate it all and wanted more.
s.fr: Gulliver mangea tout et voulut davantage.

s.t: The people brought him a strange drink, and it was sweet.
s.fr: Les gens lui apportèrent une boisson étrange, et elle était douce.

s.t: Gulliver drank and drank, and soon he slept.
s.fr: Gulliver but et but, et bientôt il dormit.

s.t: The little people had put a sleep powder in the sweet drink.
s.fr: Les petites gens avaient mis une poudre soporifique dans la boisson douce.

paras.summary: The little people bring the giant meat and bread, which he eats hungrily, and a sweet drink with a sleep powder hidden in it, so Gulliver falls asleep.

s.t: They wanted to take the giant to the great city in his sleep.
s.fr: Ils voulaient transporter le géant à la grande cité pendant son sommeil.

s.t: The people of the land built a great cart for the giant.
s.fr: Les gens du pays construisirent une grand charrette pour le géant.

s.t: 900 men with ropes lifted Gulliver up on the cart.
s.fr: 900 hommes avec des cordes soulevèrent Gulliver sur la charrette.

s.t: 1500 small horses pulled the cart, and the horses were smaller than a hand.
s.fr: 1500 petits chevaux tirèrent la charrette, et les chevaux étaient plus petits qu’une main.

s.t: They pulled the great cart for a night and a day to the city.
s.fr: Ils tirèrent la grande charrette pendant une nuit et un jour jusqu’à la ville.

paras.summary: To move the sleeping giant, the people build a great cart; 900 men lift him onto it with ropes, and 1500 tiny horses pull the cart to the city for a night and a day.

s.t: In the city was an old temple, and no house in the land was as great.
s.fr: Dans la ville se trouvait un vieux temple, et aucune maison du pays n’était aussi grande.

s.t: The people put 91 small chains on one of Gulliver's legs, and the chains held him.
s.fr: Les gens mirent 91 petites chaînes sur une des jambes de Gulliver, et les chaînes le retinrent.

s.t: When Gulliver woke, he could stand up and walk, but not far.
s.fr: Quand Gulliver se réveilla, il pouvait se lever et marcher, mais pas loin.

s.t: People came from all the land to look at the giant in the chains.
s.fr: Des gens vinrent de tout le pays pour regarder le géant dans les chaînes.

s.t: At night, Gulliver lay down in the old temple and slept.
s.fr: La nuit, Gulliver s’allongea dans le vieux temple et dormit.

paras.summary: At an old temple, the greatest house in the land, they fix 91 small chains to Gulliver's leg; he wakes able to stand and walk a little, people come from all over to look at him, and at night he sleeps in the temple.

s.t: The king of the land came to see the giant.
s.fr: Le roi du pays vint voir le géant.

s.t: The land was called Lilliput.
s.fr: Le pays s’appelait Lilliput.

s.t: The king stood a little taller than his lords.
s.fr: Le roi était un peu plus grand que ses seigneurs.

s.t: He looked at the giant's face, at his hands, and at his feet.
s.fr: Il regarda le visage du géant, ses mains, et ses pieds.

paras.summary: The king of Lilliput, a little taller than his lords, comes to the temple and looks the giant over from head to feet.

s.t: The king told the farmers of the land to bring the giant food for 1000 men.
s.fr: Le roi dit aux fermiers du pays d’apporter de la nourriture au géant pour 1000 hommes.

s.t: Each day, 40 carts of meat and bread came to the temple, and Gulliver ate it all.
s.fr: Chaque jour, 40 chariots de viande et de pain vinrent au temple, et Gulliver mangea tout.

s.t: In 30 days, Gulliver learned to speak the words of Lilliput.
s.fr: En 30 jours, Gulliver apprit à parler les mots de Lilliput.

paras.summary: The king orders the farmers to bring food each day, and in thirty days Gulliver learns to speak the words of Lilliput, asking the people for more words every day.

s.t: Little people climbed up Gulliver's arm and stood on his hand.
s.fr: De petites gens grimpèrent sur le bras de Gulliver et se tinrent sur sa main.

s.t: "Set me free," Gulliver asked the king one day.
s.fr: « Libérez-moi, » demanda Gulliver au roi un jour.

s.t: The king said that two lords must first look in Gulliver's pockets.
s.fr: Le roi dit que deux seigneurs devaient d’abord regarder dans les poches de Gulliver.

s.t: Gulliver lifted the two lords up in one hand to his pockets.
s.fr: Gulliver souleva les deux seigneurs dans une main jusqu’à ses poches.

paras.summary: The little people grow to trust Gulliver, climbing up to stand and laugh on his hand; when he asks the king to set him free, the king first sends two lords to look in his pockets, and Gulliver lifts them up himself.

s.t: The lords found a knife and gold coins.
s.fr: Les seigneurs trouvèrent un couteau et des pièces d’or.

s.t: In one more pocket, the lords found Gulliver's watch.
s.fr: Dans une autre poche, les seigneurs trouvèrent la montre de Gulliver.

s.t: The watch made a small noise over and over.
s.fr: La montre faisait un petit bruit encore et encore.

s.t: The lords stood on Gulliver's hand to look at the watch.
s.fr: Les seigneurs se tinrent sur la main de Gulliver pour regarder la montre.

s.t: They thought the watch was the god of the giant.
s.fr: Ils pensèrent que la montre était le dieu du géant.

s.t: The king let Gulliver have it all.
s.fr: Le roi laissa Gulliver avoir tout cela.

s.t: The king said Gulliver could be free after one more promise.
s.fr: Le roi dit que Gulliver pourrait être libre après une promesse de plus.

paras.summary: The lords find a knife, gold coins, and a watch that makes a small noise over and over, which they think is the giant's god; the king lets Gulliver keep everything and says one more promise will make him free.

chapterList.title: The Promise and the Egg War

s.t: The king came again to the temple with his men.
s.fr: Le roi vint de nouveau au temple avec ses hommes.

s.t: "I will walk with care in your city," said Gulliver.
s.fr: « Je marcherai avec soin dans votre ville, » dit Gulliver.

s.t: "And I will help the land of Lilliput in war," he said.
s.fr: « Et j’aiderai la terre de Lilliput en guerre, » dit-il.

s.t: The king's men took the 91 chains from Gulliver's leg.
s.fr: Les hommes du roi prirent les 91 chaînes de la jambe de Gulliver.

paras.summary: Gulliver promises the king to walk with care in the city and to help Lilliput in war, and the king has the 91 chains taken from his leg.

s.t: He walked with great care over the little city.
s.fr: Il marcha avec grand soin au-dessus de la petite ville.

s.t: He went over the city wall, for the wall was smaller than his leg.
s.fr: Il passa par-dessus le mur de la ville, car le mur était plus petit que sa jambe.

s.t: Across the sea lay one more land, Blefuscu.
s.fr: De l’autre côté de la mer se trouvait une autre terre, Blefuscu.

s.t: From the wall, Gulliver could see the ships of Blefuscu on the sea.
s.fr: Du mur, Gulliver pouvait voir les navires de Blefuscu sur la mer.

s.t: The two little lands were enemies.
s.fr: Les deux petits pays étaient ennemis.

s.t: Lilliput and Blefuscu had fought for years over which end of an egg to break first.
s.fr: Lilliput et Blefuscu s’étaient battus pendant des années sur quel bout d’un œuf casser en premier.

paras.summary: Free at last, Gulliver walks carefully over the little city and crosses the low city wall; across the sea lies Blefuscu, an enemy land whose ships he can see from the wall, for the two lands have fought for years over which end of an egg to break first.

s.t: "The ships of Blefuscu will soon come over the sea," the king said to Gulliver.
s.fr: « Les navires de Blefuscu viendront bientôt sur la mer, » dit le roi à Gulliver.

s.t: "50 great ships of war lie on the sea at Blefuscu."
s.fr: « 50 grands navires de guerre se trouvent sur la mer à Blefuscu. »

s.t: "Will you help Lilliput, as you promised?" asked the king.
s.fr: « Voulez-vous aider Lilliput, comme vous l’avez promis ? » demanda le roi.

s.t: Gulliver carried the king to the sea in his hand.
s.fr: Gulliver porta le roi jusqu’à la mer dans sa main.

s.t: The sea between the two lands was not deep for a giant.
s.fr: La mer entre les deux pays n’était pas profonde pour un géant.

s.t: "I will bring you the ships of Blefuscu," said Gulliver.
s.fr: « Je vais vous apporter les navires de Blefuscu, » dit Gulliver.

paras.summary: The king says fifty ships of war lie ready at Blefuscu and asks Gulliver to keep his promise; Gulliver carries the king down to the sea, sees the water between the lands is not deep for a giant, and promises to bring back the enemy ships, and the king shouts and laughs in his hand.

s.t: The men of Lilliput brought iron, and Gulliver made 50 great hooks.
s.fr: Les hommes de Lilliput apportèrent du fer, et Gulliver fabriqua 50 grands crochets.

s.t: He tied one of the 50 ropes to each hook.
s.fr: Il attacha une des 50 cordes à chaque crochet.

s.t: Gulliver walked into the sea between the two lands.
s.fr: Gulliver marcha dans la mer entre les deux terres.

s.t: In the deep water, the sea came up over his chest.
s.fr: Dans l’eau profonde, la mer monta jusqu’à sa poitrine.

s.t: He held the hooks and ropes over the water.
s.fr: Il tint les crochets et les cordes au-dessus de l’eau.

paras.summary: Gulliver makes fifty iron hooks, ties a rope to each, and walks into the sea between the two lands, holding the hooks and ropes over the water where the sea comes up over his chest.

s.t: The men of Blefuscu saw the giant come through the sea.
s.fr: Les hommes de Blefuscu virent le géant traverser la mer.

s.t: They jumped from their ships into the sea and swam to the shore.
s.fr: Ils sautèrent de leurs navires dans la mer et nagèrent vers le rivage.

s.t: 1000 arrows came down on Gulliver's hands and face.
s.fr: 1000 flèches tombèrent sur les mains et le visage de Gulliver.

s.t: The little arrows hurt, but Gulliver walked on.
s.fr: Les petites flèches faisaient mal, mais Gulliver continua à marcher.

paras.summary: The men of Blefuscu jump from their ships and swim ashore when they see the giant coming, and though a thousand little arrows hurt his hands and face, Gulliver walks on.

s.t: At the ships of Blefuscu, he put one hook on each ship.
s.fr: Près des navires de Blefuscu, il posa un crochet sur chaque navire.

s.t: But the ships did not move, for the anchors held.
s.fr: Mais les navires ne bougèrent pas, car les ancres tenaient.

s.t: Gulliver took his knife and cut the anchor ropes one by one.
s.fr: Gulliver prit son couteau et coupa les cordes d’ancre une par une.

s.t: He held the ends of all 50 ropes in one hand.
s.fr: Il tint les extrémités de toutes les 50 cordes dans une main.

s.t: Gulliver turned and pulled the 50 ships after him through the sea.
s.fr: Gulliver se retourna et tira les 50 navires derrière lui à travers la mer.

paras.summary: Gulliver puts a hook on each ship, cuts the anchor ropes with his knife when the anchors hold the ships fast, gathers all fifty ropes in one hand, and pulls the ships after him through the sea.

s.t: The king of Lilliput stood on his shore and watched the ships come.
s.fr: Le roi de Lilliput se tint sur son rivage et regarda les navires arriver.

s.t: "One man took all the ships of Blefuscu!" said the king.
s.fr: « Un homme a pris tous les navires de Blefuscu ! » dit le roi.

s.t: He made Gulliver the first lord of Lilliput that day.
s.fr: Il fit de Gulliver le premier seigneur de Lilliput ce jour-là.

paras.summary: The people of Blefuscu shout from their shore while the king of Lilliput watches the ships come; the king says one man has taken all the ships of Blefuscu, makes Gulliver the first lord of the land, and that night the people make great fires on the shore.

s.t: The king of Blefuscu sent men over the sea to ask for peace.
s.fr: Le roi de Blefuscu envoya des hommes par la mer pour demander la paix.

s.t: Lilliput and Blefuscu made peace, and the war of the eggs was over.
s.fr: Lilliput et Blefuscu firent la paix, et la guerre des œufs était terminée.

s.t: But the king of Lilliput wanted more than peace.
s.fr: Mais le roi de Lilliput voulait plus que la paix.

s.t: "Take all of Blefuscu for me," the king said to Gulliver.
s.fr: « Prenez tout Blefuscu pour moi, » dit le roi à Gulliver.

s.t: "Their land will be my land, and their people will be my people."
s.fr: « Leur terre sera ma terre, et leur peuple sera mon peuple. »

paras.summary: Blefuscu asks for peace and the egg war ends, but the king of Lilliput wants more: he tells Gulliver to take all of Blefuscu so that its land and people will be his.

s.t: Gulliver looked down at the little king.
s.fr: Gulliver regarda en bas le petit roi.

s.t: "No," said Gulliver.
s.fr: « Non, » dit Gulliver.

s.t: "The people of Blefuscu are a free people, and I will not take their land."
s.fr: « Les gens de Blefuscu sont un peuple libre, et je ne prendrai pas leur terre. »

s.t: The king said no more, but from that day he did not laugh with Gulliver.
s.fr: Le roi ne dit plus rien, mais à partir de ce jour il ne rit plus avec Gulliver.

paras.summary: Gulliver looks down at the little king and says no, for the people of Blefuscu are a free people; the king says no more, but from that day he does not laugh with Gulliver.

s.t: One night, the people of the city came calling to the temple.
s.fr: Une nuit, les gens de la ville vinrent appeler au temple.

s.t: "Fire, fire!" the people called.
s.fr: « Feu, feu ! » crièrent les gens.

s.t: "The queen's rooms are on fire!"
s.fr: « Les chambres de la reine sont en feu ! »

s.t: Gulliver ran to the palace with great care for the little houses.
s.fr: Gulliver courut au palais avec grand soin pour les petites maisons.

s.t: The people threw little buckets of water on the fire, but the fire grew.
s.fr: Les gens jetèrent de petits seaux d’eau sur le feu, mais le feu grandit.

paras.summary: One night the people come calling that the queen's rooms are on fire; Gulliver runs carefully to the palace, where little buckets of water cannot stop the growing fire.

s.t: The sea was not far, and Gulliver had his great hat.
s.fr: La mer n’était pas loin, et Gulliver avait son grand chapeau.

s.t: He filled the hat with sea water and threw the water on the fire.
s.fr: Il remplit le chapeau d’eau de mer et jeta l’eau sur le feu.

s.t: He went to the sea and came back, again and again.
s.fr: Il alla à la mer et revint, encore et encore.

s.t: Soon the fire was out, and the palace still stood.
s.fr: Bientôt le feu fut éteint, et le palais tenait encore debout.

s.t: But sea water lay over all the rooms of the queen.
s.fr: Mais l’eau de mer couvrait toutes les chambres de la reine.

s.t: The queen did not laugh with Gulliver again.
s.fr: La reine ne rit plus avec Gulliver.

paras.summary: Gulliver fills his great hat with sea water and throws it on the fire, going back to the sea again and again until the fire is out; the palace stands, but sea water lies over all the queen's rooms, and the queen does not laugh with Gulliver again.

s.t: After the fire, some lords of the court wanted the giant gone.
s.fr: Après l’incendie, certains seigneurs de la cour voulaient le géant parti.

s.t: "The giant eats the food of 1000 men," said one lord.
s.fr: « Le géant mange la nourriture de 1000 hommes, » dit un seigneur.

s.t: "He would not take Blefuscu for his king," said the queen.
s.fr: « Il ne prendrait pas Blefuscu pour son roi, » dit la reine.

s.t: The court said the giant must be tied down again, for all his days.
s.fr: La cour dit que le géant devait être attaché de nouveau, pour tous ses jours.

paras.summary: After the fire, lords of the court want the giant gone — he eats the food of 1000 men, and he would not take Blefuscu for his king — and the court says he must be tied down again for all his days.

s.t: But one lord of the court was Gulliver's friend.
s.fr: Mais un seigneur de la cour était l’ami de Gulliver.

s.t: That night, the friend came alone in the dark to the temple.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, l’ami vint seul dans l’obscurité jusqu’au temple.

s.t: The giant put the friend up on his hand.
s.fr: Le géant posa l’ami sur sa main.

s.t: "The court will put you in chains again," said the friend.
s.fr: « La cour va vous mettre · de nouveau dans les chaînes, » dit l’ami.

s.t: "Go from Lilliput this night."
s.fr: Pars de Lilliput cette nuit.

paras.summary: One lord who is Gulliver's friend comes alone through the dark to the temple and warns him: the court will put him in chains again, so he must go from Lilliput that night.

s.t: Gulliver did not want a war with the little people of the land.
s.fr: Gulliver ne voulait pas la guerre avec les petits peuples du pays.

s.t: He thanked the friend and put him down on the ground.
s.fr: Il remercia l’ami et le posa par terre.

s.t: In the dark, Gulliver walked into the sea and went over to Blefuscu.
s.fr: Dans l’obscurité, Gulliver entra dans la mer et alla vers Blefuscu.

s.t: The king of Blefuscu came to the shore with many of his little people.
s.fr: Le roi de Blefuscu vint au rivage avec beaucoup de ses petits peuples.

paras.summary: Gulliver does not want a war with the little people, so he thanks the friend and walks through the dark sea over to Blefuscu, where the king comes to the shore with his people.

s.t: He was glad to see the man that had not taken his land.
s.fr: Il était content de voir l’homme qui n’avait pas pris sa terre.

s.t: "You will be safe in Blefuscu," said the king of Blefuscu.
s.fr: « Vous serez en sécurité à Blefuscu, » dit le roi de Blefuscu.

s.t: The people of Blefuscu brought the giant food each day.
s.fr: Les peuples de Blefuscu apportèrent de la nourriture au géant chaque jour.

s.t: But at night, Gulliver looked over the sea and wanted to go home to England.
s.fr: Mais la nuit, Gulliver regardait la mer et voulait rentrer chez lui en Angleterre.

paras.summary: The king of Blefuscu, glad to see the man that did not take his land, tells Gulliver he is safe, and his people bring the giant food each day; but at night Gulliver looks over the sea and wants to go home to England.

s.t: One day, Gulliver saw a real boat far out on the sea.
s.fr: Un jour, Gulliver vit un vrai bateau loin sur la mer.

s.t: It was a boat from a great ship, and the sea had turned it over.
s.fr: C’était un bateau d’un grand navire, et la mer l’avait retourné.

s.t: The wind drove the boat into the shallow water, and Gulliver swam out to it.
s.fr: Le vent poussa le bateau vers les eaux peu profondes, et Gulliver nagea jusqu’à lui.

s.t: With 2000 men of Blefuscu and many ropes, he turned the boat over in the water.
s.fr: Avec 2000 hommes de Blefuscu et beaucoup de cordes, il retourna le bateau dans l’eau.

s.t: The king of Blefuscu gave Gulliver wood, and soon the boat was good again.
s.fr: Le roi de Blefuscu donna à Gulliver du bois, et bientôt le bateau était de nouveau.

paras.summary: Gulliver sees a real boat from a great ship floating turned over far out on the sea; the wind drives it near, and with 2000 men and many ropes he turns it over, and the king gives him wood to make it good again.

s.t: The people of Blefuscu brought meat, bread, and milk for the long way home.
s.fr: Les gens de Blefuscu apportèrent de la viande, du pain, et du lait pour le long chemin du retour.

s.t: Gulliver took 6 little cows of Blefuscu into the boat too.
s.fr: Gulliver prit aussi 6 petites vaches de Blefuscu dans le bateau.

s.t: He wanted to show England the little cows.
s.fr: Il voulait montrer à l’Angleterre les petites vaches.

s.t: Gulliver thanked the king of Blefuscu and sailed away.
s.fr: Gulliver remercia le roi de Blefuscu et navigua au loin.

paras.summary: The people of Blefuscu bring meat, bread, and milk for the long way home; Gulliver takes six little cows into the boat to show England, thanks the king, and sails away.

s.t: After two days on the sea, Gulliver saw a great ship.
s.fr: Après deux jours sur la mer, Gulliver vit un grand navire.

s.t: It was a ship from England, with men as great as Gulliver.
s.fr: C’était un navire d’Angleterre, avec des hommes aussi grands que Gulliver.

s.t: The men of the ship took Gulliver and his boat up from the sea.
s.fr: Les hommes du navire prirent Gulliver et son bateau hors de la mer.

s.t: Gulliver told the captain of Lilliput, and the captain laughed.
s.fr: Gulliver parla au capitaine de Lilliput, et le capitaine rit.

s.t: Gulliver went to his boat and took out one little cow.
s.fr: Gulliver alla à son bateau et en sortit une petite vache.

s.t: He put the little cow in the captain's hand.
s.fr: Il posa la petite vache dans la main du capitaine.

s.t: The captain looked at it and laughed no more.
s.fr: Le capitaine le regarda et ne rit plus.

paras.summary: After two days he meets a ship from England full of men as great as himself; the captain laughs at his words about Lilliput, so Gulliver fetches a little cow from his boat and puts it in the captain's hand, and the captain laughs no more.

s.t: The ship sailed home, and Gulliver came to his house in England.
s.fr: Le navire rentra chez lui, et Gulliver arriva à sa maison en Angleterre.

s.t: His wife had thought the sea had taken him, and she laughed and cried to see him.
s.fr: Sa femme avait cru que la mer l’avait emporté, et elle rit et pleura de joie en le voyant.

s.t: Gulliver stayed at home for 60 days.
s.fr: Gulliver resta chez lui pendant 60 jours.

s.t: But he still thought of the sea and far lands.
s.fr: Mais il pensait encore à la mer et aux terres lointaines.

paras.summary: The ship sails home to England, where Gulliver's wife, who thought the sea had taken him, laughs and cries to see him; he stays home for sixty days, but he still thinks of the sea and far lands.

s.t: When the 60 days were over, a new ship sailed from England.
s.fr: Quand les 60 jours furent passés, un nouveau navire quitta l’Angleterre.

s.t: Gulliver went with it, for he still wanted to see far lands.
s.fr: Gulliver l’accompagna, car il voulait encore voir des terres lointaines.

s.t: Far out on the sea, a great storm drove the ship for many days.
s.fr: Loin sur la mer, une grande tempête poussa le navire pendant de nombreux jours.

s.t: No man on the ship knew the way home.
s.fr: Aucun homme sur le navire ne connaissait le chemin du retour.

paras.summary: After sixty days at home, Gulliver sails again on a new ship, but a great storm drives it far over the sea until no man knows the way home.

s.t: When the storm was over, the men saw a strange land.
s.fr: Quand la tempête fut passée, les hommes aperçurent une terre étrange.

s.t: The men wanted water, so the captain sent a boat to the shore.
s.fr: Les hommes voulaient de l’eau, alors le capitaine envoya un bateau vers le rivage.

s.t: Gulliver went with the boat and walked alone over the strange land.
s.fr: Gulliver monta dans le bateau et marcha seul sur cette terre étrange.

s.t: He walked a mile from the shore and saw no man and no house.
s.fr: Il marcha à un mile du rivage et ne vit ni homme ni maison.

paras.summary: They see a strange land, and the captain sends a boat for water; Gulliver walks alone far from the shore and finds no man and no house.

s.t: When Gulliver came back, the boat was far out on the water.
s.fr: Quand Gulliver revint, le bateau était loin sur l’eau.

s.t: The men in the boat rowed fast for the ship.
s.fr: Les hommes dans le bateau ramèrent vite vers le navire.

s.t: A giant man walked in the sea after the boat.
s.fr: Un homme géant marcha dans la mer après le bateau.

s.t: The sea came only to the giant's knees.
s.fr: La mer arrivait seulement aux genoux du géant.

s.t: The giant was as tall as a ship's mast.
s.fr: Le géant était aussi grand que le mât d’un navire.

s.t: Gulliver called from the shore, but the boat did not come back.
s.fr: Gulliver appela depuis le rivage, mais le bateau ne revint pas.

paras.summary: When he comes back, the boat is racing for the ship, for a giant man is walking after it through a sea that only comes to his knees; Gulliver calls from the shore, but the boat does not come back.

s.t: He ran from the sea into the land.
s.fr: Il courut de la mer vers l’intérieur des terres.

s.t: Gulliver came to a great field of yellow grain.
s.fr: Gulliver arriva à un grand champ de grain jaune.

s.t: The grain stood far over his head, as tall as the trees of England.
s.fr: Le grain s’élevait bien au-dessus de sa tête, aussi grand que les arbres d’Angleterre.

s.t: He heard great feet come through the grain, and he hid and waited.
s.fr: Il entendit de grands pas traverser le grain, et il se cacha et attendit.

paras.summary: Gulliver runs inland to a field of grain that stands as tall as the trees of England; in Lilliput he was the giant, but in this new land he is the little man, and when he hears great feet coming through the grain, he hides and waits.

s.t: Giant men came through the field and cut down the tall grain.
s.fr: Des hommes géants traversèrent le champ et coupèrent le grand grain.

s.t: Great feet came down in the tall grain by Gulliver's head.
s.fr: De grands pieds s’abattirent sur le grand grain près de la tête de Gulliver.

s.t: Gulliver called and called up at the giant men.
s.fr: Gulliver appela et appela encore les hommes géants.

s.t: The great feet stood still in the grain.
s.fr: Les grands pieds s’immobilisèrent dans le grain.

s.t: The farmer of the field looked down and saw the little man in the grain.
s.fr: Le fermier du champ regarda en bas et vit le petit homme dans le grain.

paras.summary: Giant men come cutting the grain, and when great feet come down by his head, Gulliver calls and calls; the feet stop, and the farmer of the field looks down and sees him.

s.t: The farmer took Gulliver up between his finger and his thumb.
s.fr: Le fermier prit Gulliver entre son doigt et son pouce.

s.t: He lifted the little man high over the field to look at him.
s.fr: Il souleva le petit homme haut au-dessus du champ pour le regarder.

s.t: Gulliver held the great thumb, for the ground was far down.
s.fr: Gulliver tint le grand pouce, car le sol était loin en bas.

s.t: Gulliver bowed in the great hand and spoke, but the farmer could not understand the little words.
s.fr: Gulliver s’inclina dans la grande main et parla, mais le fermier ne pouvait pas comprendre les petits mots.

paras.summary: The farmer takes Gulliver up between finger and thumb and lifts him high over the field; far above the ground, Gulliver holds the great thumb, bows in the great hand, and speaks, but the farmer cannot understand the little words.

s.t: The farmer put Gulliver in his pocket and carried him home.
s.fr: Le fermier mit Gulliver dans sa poche et le porta chez lui.

s.t: At the house, the farmer took Gulliver from the pocket and put him on the table.
s.fr: À la maison, le fermier sortit Gulliver de la poche et le posa sur la table.

s.t: The farmer's wife saw the little man, and her cup fell from her hand.
s.fr: La femme du fermier vit le petit homme, et sa tasse tomba de sa main.

s.t: But Gulliver bowed to her too, and soon she laughed.
s.fr: Mais Gulliver s’inclina devant elle aussi, et bientôt elle rit.

paras.summary: The farmer carries Gulliver home in his pocket and puts him on the table, where the farmer's wife drops her cup at the sight, but Gulliver bows to her too and soon she laughs.

s.t: The farmer and his wife sat down at the table with bread and milk.
s.fr: Le fermier et sa femme s’assirent à la table avec du pain et du lait.

s.t: Gulliver drank milk from the smallest cup of the house, and the cup was as great as a bucket.
s.fr: Gulliver but du lait dans la plus petite tasse de la maison, et la tasse était aussi grande qu’un seau.

s.t: He fell over the bread on the table, and the giants laughed.
s.fr: Il trébucha sur le pain sur la table, et les géants rirent.

s.t: The farmer's daughter watched the little man with care.
s.fr: La fille du fermier observa le petit homme avec soin.

s.t: That night, the daughter put soft cloth in a small box for Gulliver's bed.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, la fille mit du tissu doux dans une petite boîte pour le lit de Gulliver.

s.t: In the box bed, Gulliver slept his first night in the land of the giants.
s.fr: Dans la boîte, Gulliver dormit sa première nuit dans le pays des géants.

paras.summary: At dinner Gulliver drinks milk from the smallest cup of the house, as great as a bucket, and falls over the bread while the giants laugh; the farmer's daughter watches him with care, makes him a bed of soft cloth in a small box, and Gulliver sleeps his first night in the land of the giants.

s.t: The farmer's daughter took care of Gulliver in the great house.
s.fr: La fille du fermier prit soin de Gulliver dans la grande maison.

s.t: She made him new clothes from soft cloth.
s.fr: Elle lui fit de nouveaux vêtements en tissu doux.

s.t: She set his food by his box bed and kept him safe.
s.fr: Elle posa sa nourriture près de sa boîte et le garda en sécurité.

s.t: Each day, the daughter gave Gulliver more words of the land.
s.fr: Chaque jour, la fille donna à Gulliver plus de mots du pays.

paras.summary: The farmer's daughter takes care of Gulliver, making him new clothes from soft cloth, setting his food by his box bed, keeping him safe, and giving him more words of the land each day.

s.t: She pointed at the bread, the milk, the cup, and the fire, and said each word.
s.fr: Elle pointa le pain, le lait, la tasse, et le feu, et dit chaque mot.

s.t: He learned fast, for he had learned the words of Lilliput too.
s.fr: Il apprit vite, car il avait appris les mots de Lilliput aussi.

s.t: Soon the little man could speak with the daughter.
s.fr: Bientôt le petit homme put parler avec la fille.

paras.summary: She points at things and says each word, and Gulliver says the words after her; he learns fast, since he once learned the words of Lilliput, and soon they can speak together.

s.t: "This land is Brobdingnag," said the daughter.
s.fr: « Cette terre est Brobdingnag, » dit la fille.

s.t: Gulliver told the daughter of England and of little Lilliput.
s.fr: Gulliver parla à la fille de l’Angleterre et du petit Lilliput.

s.t: One day, an old farmer came to the house to see the little man.
s.fr: Un jour, un vieux fermier vint à la maison pour voir le petit homme.

s.t: Gulliver walked on the table, bowed, and spoke to him.
s.fr: Gulliver marcha sur la table, s’inclina, et lui parla.

paras.summary: The daughter tells him the land is called Brobdingnag, and Gulliver tells her of England and of little Lilliput, and she laughs at the thought of a land where Gulliver was the giant; then an old farmer comes to see the little man, and Gulliver walks, bows, and speaks for him.

s.t: The old farmer looked and looked at the little man.
s.fr: Le vieux fermier regarda et regarda le petit homme.

s.t: "Show the little man at the market for money," the old farmer said.
s.fr: « Montrez le petit homme au marché pour de l’argent, » dit le vieux fermier.

s.t: The farmer of the house heard him and thought of the money.
s.fr: Le fermier de la maison l’entendit et pensa à l’argent.

s.t: "The little man will go to the market," said the farmer of the house.
s.fr: « Le petit homme ira au marché, » dit le fermier de la maison.

s.t: The daughter was afraid for Gulliver, so she said she would go too.
s.fr: La fille avait peur pour Gulliver, alors elle dit qu’elle irait aussi.

s.t: The daughter set more soft cloth in Gulliver's box for the market.
s.fr: La fille mit plus de tissu doux dans la boîte de Gulliver pour le marché.

paras.summary: The old farmer looks and looks and says to show the little man at the market for money; the farmer thinks of the money and agrees, and the daughter, afraid for Gulliver, says she will go too and sets more soft cloth in his box for the way.

s.t: On market day, the farmer rode his horse to the market town.
s.fr: Le jour du marché, le fermier chevaucha son cheval jusqu’au bourg du marché.

s.t: The daughter held Gulliver's box with great care on the way.
s.fr: La fille tint la boîte de Gulliver avec grand soin pendant le trajet.

s.t: At the market, the farmer set the box on a great table.
s.fr: Au marché, le fermier posa la boîte sur une grande table.

s.t: "Come and see the little man from the sea!" called the farmer.
s.fr: « Venez voir le petit homme de la mer ! » cria le fermier.

s.t: The people of the town paid the farmer silver coins and came in to look.
s.fr: Les gens de la ville payèrent au fermier des pièces d’argent et entrèrent pour regarder.

paras.summary: On market day the farmer rides to town while the daughter holds Gulliver's box with care; at the market he sets the box on a table, calls the people in, and they pay silver coins to look.

s.t: Gulliver walked up and down the table and bowed to the crowd.
s.fr: Gulliver fit des allers-retours sur la table et s’inclina devant la foule.

s.t: He spoke the words of the land, and the crowd watched with open mouths.
s.fr: Il prononça les mots de la région, et la foule regarda avec des bouches ouvertes.

s.t: He drank from a little cup, and the crowd laughed and paid more.
s.fr: Il but dans une petite coupe, et la foule rit et paya davantage.

s.t: The farmer looked at all the silver and laughed.
s.fr: Le fermier regarda tout l’argent et rit.

paras.summary: Gulliver walks, bows, speaks the words of the land, and drinks from a little cup while the crowd watches with open mouths and pays more, and the farmer looks at all the silver and laughs.

s.t: After that, the farmer showed Gulliver at market after market.
s.fr: Après cela, le fermier montra Gulliver à marché après marché.

s.t: They went from town to town for many weeks.
s.fr: Ils allèrent de ville en ville pendant de nombreuses semaines.

s.t: He could not rest, and he could not sleep.
s.fr: Il ne pouvait pas se reposer, et il ne pouvait pas dormir.

s.t: Gulliver grew thin and tired and weak.
s.fr: Gulliver devint mince et fatigué et faible.

paras.summary: The farmer shows Gulliver at market after market, town after town, week after week; the show runs from morning to night, and with no rest and no sleep Gulliver grows thin and tired and weak.

s.t: In the end, the farmer took Gulliver to the great city of the land.
s.fr: À la fin, le fermier emmena Gulliver dans la grande ville du pays.

s.t: The king and queen of the giants lived there, in a palace of high walls.
s.fr: Le roi et la reine des géants vivaient là, dans un palais aux murs hauts.

s.t: Soon the queen heard of the little man and called for him to the palace.
s.fr: Bientôt la reine entendit parler du petit homme et le fit appeler au palais.

paras.summary: The daughter takes more care of the tired little man; in the end the farmer takes Gulliver to the great city, where the king and queen of the giants live in a palace of high walls, and soon the queen hears of the little man and calls for him.

s.t: The farmer carried Gulliver's box to the palace of the queen.
s.fr: Le fermier porta la boîte de Gulliver au palais de la reine.

s.t: Gulliver walked out of the box and bowed to the queen of the giants.
s.fr: Gulliver sortit de la boîte et s’inclina devant la reine des géants.

s.t: "Will you make your home at my palace?" the queen asked the little man.
s.fr: « Voulez-vous faire votre maison dans mon palais ? » demanda la reine au petit homme.

s.t: "I will come if the daughter comes too, for she takes care of me," said Gulliver.
s.fr: « Je viendrai si la fille vient aussi, car elle s’occupe de moi », dit Gulliver.

s.t: The queen was glad to let the daughter come.
s.fr: La reine fut heureuse de laisser la fille venir.

paras.summary: The farmer carries Gulliver's box to the palace, where Gulliver bows to the queen; he agrees to come if the farmer's daughter can come too, since she takes care of him, and the queen gladly lets her stay.

s.t: The queen bought Gulliver from the farmer for 1000 gold coins.
s.fr: La reine acheta Gulliver au fermier pour 1000 pièces d’or.

s.t: The farmer took the gold, laughed, and rode home.
s.fr: Le fermier prit l’or, rit, et rentra chez lui.

s.t: The queen's men built Gulliver a little room of wood.
s.fr: Les hommes de la reine construisirent à Gulliver une petite chambre de bois.

s.t: The little room had a door, two windows, a table, a chair, and a bed.
s.fr: La petite chambre avait une porte, deux fenêtres, une table, une chaise, et un lit.

s.t: The queen's men put soft cloth on the walls of the room.
s.fr: Les hommes de la reine posèrent du tissu doux sur les murs de la chambre.

s.t: On the roof of the room, the men put a great iron ring.
s.fr: Sur le toit de la chambre, les hommes posèrent un grand anneau de fer.

s.t: The daughter took the ring and carried the box from room to room.
s.fr: La fille prit l’anneau et porta la boîte de chambre en chambre.

paras.summary: The queen buys Gulliver for 1000 gold coins, and the farmer rides home with the gold; the queen's men build Gulliver a little wooden room with a door, two windows, a table, a chair, and a bed, put soft cloth on its walls, and fix a great iron ring on the roof so the daughter can carry the box from room to room.

s.t: One day, the king of the giants came to see the queen's little man.
s.fr: Un jour, le roi des géants vint voir le petit homme de la reine.

s.t: The king thought the queen's little man was a toy.
s.fr: Le roi pensa que le petit homme de la reine était un jouet.

s.t: But the toy bowed and asked the king about his great land.
s.fr: Mais le jouet s’inclina et demanda au roi à propos de sa grande terre.

s.t: The king asked Gulliver 100 questions, and Gulliver answered each one.
s.fr: Le roi posa à Gulliver 100 questions, et Gulliver répondit à chacune.

s.t: Gulliver spoke of the wars of England, and the king laughed and laughed.
s.fr: Gulliver parla des guerres d’Angleterre, et le roi rit et rit.

s.t: "So small a people, and so great a war!" said the king of the giants.
s.fr: « Un peuple si petit, et une si grande guerre ! » dit le roi des géants.

paras.summary: The king of the giants thinks the queen's little man a toy, until the toy bows and speaks; the king asks 100 questions, laughs and laughs at the wars of England — so small a people, so great a war — and at night Gulliver sleeps in his own little bed in the palace.

s.t: Each day, Gulliver ate dinner at the queen's great table.
s.fr: Chaque jour, Gulliver dînait à la grande table de la reine.

s.t: His little chair and table stood by the queen's great plate.
s.fr: Sa petite chaise et sa table se trouvaient près de la grande assiette de la reine.

s.t: A dwarf lived at the court of the queen too.
s.fr: Un nain vivait à la cour de la reine aussi.

s.t: Before Gulliver came, the dwarf was the smallest man of the court.
s.fr: Avant que Gulliver arrive, le nain était le plus petit homme de la cour.

s.t: But the court only watched Gulliver now, and no one watched the dwarf.
s.fr: Mais la cour ne regardait que Gulliver maintenant, et personne ne regardait le nain.

s.t: The dwarf was angry at the little man.
s.fr: Le nain était en colère contre le petit homme.

paras.summary: Gulliver eats dinner each day at the queen's table, where a dwarf, once the smallest man of the court, grows angry because the court now watches only Gulliver.

s.t: One day at dinner, a great silver bowl of sweet cream stood on the table.
s.fr: Un jour à dîner, un grand bol d’argent plein de crème sucrée se trouvait sur la table.

s.t: The cream in the bowl was deep for a little man.
s.fr: La crème dans le bol était profonde pour un petit homme.

s.t: The dwarf took Gulliver from his chair and dropped him into the cream.
s.fr: Le nain prit Gulliver de sa chaise et le laissa tomber dans la crème.

s.t: Gulliver went down into the deep cream.
s.fr: Gulliver descendit dans la crème profonde.

s.t: But Gulliver had swum in the great sea, and he could swim in cream.
s.fr: Mais Gulliver avait nagé dans la grande mer, et il pouvait nager dans la crème.

s.t: He held his head up and swam in the cream.
s.fr: Il maintint sa tête au-dessus et nagea dans la crème.

paras.summary: At dinner one day, the dwarf drops Gulliver from his chair into a great silver bowl of sweet cream; the cream is deep for a little man, but Gulliver has swum in the great sea, and he swims with his head up.

s.t: The daughter saw him and ran to the table.
s.fr: La fille le vit et courut à la table.

s.t: She put her great spoon into the cream, and Gulliver climbed on.
s.fr: Elle plongea sa grande cuillère dans la crème, et Gulliver monta dessus.

s.t: The daughter lifted Gulliver out and made him dry with soft cloth.
s.fr: La fille sortit Gulliver et le sécha avec un tissu doux.

s.t: The queen was angry at the dwarf.
s.fr: La reine était en colère contre le nain.

s.t: She sent the dwarf away from the court that day.
s.fr: Elle renvoya le nain de la cour ce jour-là.

s.t: But after that, the daughter watched Gulliver with more care at dinner.
s.fr: Mais après cela, la fille surveilla Gulliver avec plus de soin au dîner.

paras.summary: The daughter runs to the table, puts her great spoon into the cream, and lifts Gulliver out to dry him with soft cloth; the angry queen sends the dwarf away that day, Gulliver laughs about the cream with the court, and after that the daughter watches him with more care at dinner.

s.t: One warm morning, the queen called the daughter away.
s.fr: Un matin chaud, la reine appela la fille loin.

s.t: The window of Gulliver's little room stood open to the garden.
s.fr: La fenêtre de la petite chambre de Gulliver donnait ouverte sur le jardin.

s.t: A monkey lived in the trees of the palace garden.
s.fr: Un singe vivait dans les arbres du jardin du palais.

s.t: The monkey came down, ran over the wall, and climbed in at the open window.
s.fr: Le singe descendit, courut par-dessus le mur, et entra par la fenêtre ouverte.

paras.summary: One warm morning the queen calls the daughter away, and while the window of Gulliver's room stands open, a monkey from the palace garden climbs in.

s.t: It found Gulliver in the little room.
s.fr: Il trouva Gulliver dans la petite chambre.

s.t: The monkey took Gulliver up in one arm, as monkeys hold their young.
s.fr: Le singe prit Gulliver dans un bras, comme les singes tiennent leurs petits.

s.t: Gulliver saw the great teeth and could not get free.
s.fr: Gulliver vit les grandes dents et ne put pas se libérer.

s.t: It put food from its mouth into Gulliver's mouth.
s.fr: Il mit de la nourriture de sa bouche dans la bouche de Gulliver.

paras.summary: The monkey takes Gulliver up in one arm the way monkeys hold their young; Gulliver sees the great teeth and cannot get free, and the monkey even puts food from its mouth into his.

s.t: The monkey jumped out of the window with Gulliver and climbed up the palace wall.
s.fr: Le singe sauta par la fenêtre avec Gulliver et grimpa le long du mur du palais.

s.t: It ran up and up, to the top of the palace roof.
s.fr: Il courut de plus en plus haut, jusqu’au sommet du toit du palais.

s.t: The garden lay far below the little man.
s.fr: Le jardin était loin en dessous du petit homme.

s.t: Great screams came from the garden below.
s.fr: De grands cris vinrent du jardin en bas.

paras.summary: The monkey jumps out of the window, climbs the palace wall to the top of the roof with the garden far below, and people scream when they see the monkey and the man.

s.t: The daughter ran out and called for the little man.
s.fr: La fille courut dehors et appela le petit homme.

s.t: Men came with long ladders and climbed to the roof.
s.fr: Des hommes vinrent avec de longues échelles et montèrent sur le toit.

s.t: The monkey saw the men, set Gulliver down on the roof, and ran away over the wall.
s.fr: Le singe vit les hommes, posa Gulliver sur le toit, et s’enfuit par-dessus le mur.

s.t: One of the queen's men put Gulliver in his pocket and climbed down the ladder.
s.fr: Un des hommes de la reine mit Gulliver dans sa poche et descendit l’échelle.

s.t: The daughter held Gulliver, and her great tears fell on him.
s.fr: La fille tint Gulliver, et ses grandes larmes tombèrent sur lui.

s.t: Gulliver was sick for two days from the monkey's food.
s.fr: Gulliver fut malade pendant deux jours à cause de la nourriture du singe.

s.t: After that day, the window of the little room stood open no more.
s.fr: Après ce jour, la fenêtre de la petite chambre resta ouverte plus jamais.

paras.summary: The daughter cries out while men climb with long ladders; the monkey sets Gulliver down and runs away, a queen's man carries Gulliver down in his pocket, the daughter's great tears fall on him, and after two days of being sick from the monkey's food, Gulliver finds the window is never left open again.

s.t: One day, the king and queen went down to the sea and took Gulliver too.
s.fr: Un jour, le roi et la reine descendirent vers la mer et emmenèrent Gulliver aussi.

s.t: Gulliver had not seen the sea for two years, and he wanted to see the waves again.
s.fr: Gulliver n’avait pas vu la mer depuis deux ans, et il voulait revoir les vagues.

s.t: But that day the daughter was sick and could not come down to the shore.
s.fr: Mais ce jour-là, la fille était malade et ne pouvait pas descendre au rivage.

s.t: A boy carried Gulliver's box down to the rocks by the sea.
s.fr: Un garçon porta la boîte de Gulliver jusqu’aux rochers au bord de la mer.

s.t: Gulliver was tired, and he lay down on the bed in the box.
s.fr: Gulliver était fatigué, et il s’allongea sur le lit dans la boîte.

s.t: The boy set the box on the rocks and walked away to look for birds' eggs.
s.fr: Le garçon posa la boîte sur les rochers et s’éloigna pour chercher des œufs d’oiseaux.

paras.summary: The king and queen go down to the sea and take Gulliver, who has not seen the waves for two years; the daughter is sick that day, so a boy carries the box to the rocks, where tired Gulliver lies down while the boy walks away to look for birds' eggs.

s.t: Gulliver woke when great wings came down over the box.
s.fr: Gulliver se réveilla quand de grandes ailes descendirent sur la boîte.

s.t: All at once, the box rose fast into the air.
s.fr: Tout à coup, la boîte monta vite dans l’air.

s.t: An eagle had taken the box by the great iron ring.
s.fr: Un aigle avait saisi la boîte par le grand anneau de fer.

s.t: The eagle flew high over the sea with the box.
s.fr: L’aigle vola haut au-dessus de la mer avec la boîte.

s.t: Gulliver looked out of the window and saw only air and sea.
s.fr: Gulliver regarda par la fenêtre et ne vit que de l’air et de la mer.

s.t: More great wings came, and other birds flew at the eagle.
s.fr: De grandes ailes arrivèrent, et d’autres oiseaux volèrent vers l’aigle.

s.t: The eagle let the box go.
s.fr: L’aigle lâcha la boîte.

paras.summary: Gulliver wakes to great wings over the box, and all at once it rises fast into the air: an eagle has taken it by the iron ring and flies high over the sea, until other birds fly at the eagle and it lets the box go.

s.t: The box fell down and down through the air.
s.fr: La boîte tomba de plus en plus bas dans l’air.

s.t: It hit the sea and went under, but the box came up again.
s.fr: Elle heurta la mer et passa dessous, mais la boîte remonta.

s.t: The box was good dry wood, and it did not sink.
s.fr: La boîte était faite de bon bois sec, et elle ne coula pas.

s.t: Gulliver held fast in the box and was not hurt.
s.fr: Gulliver se tint fermement dans la boîte et ne fut pas blessé.

s.t: The waves lifted the box up and down on the great sea.
s.fr: Les vagues soulevèrent la boîte en haut et en bas sur la grande mer.

paras.summary: The box falls down and down, hits the sea, and comes up again, for it is good dry wood; Gulliver holds fast and is not hurt, and alone on the great sea the box rises and falls on the waves while he waits.

s.t: Men on a great ship of England saw the box on the waves.
s.fr: Des hommes sur un grand navire d’Angleterre virent la boîte sur les vagues.

s.t: Sailors came out with hooks and ropes.
s.fr: Des marins sortirent avec des crochets et des cordes.

s.t: The sailors put the hooks in the great ring and pulled the box to the ship.
s.fr: Les marins mirent les crochets dans le grand anneau et tirèrent la boîte vers le navire.

s.t: Gulliver called from the box, and the sailors answered him.
s.fr: Gulliver appela depuis la boîte, et les marins lui répondirent.

s.t: The sailors cut a hole in the roof of the box.
s.fr: Les marins découpèrent un trou dans le toit de la boîte.

s.t: Gulliver came out of the box into the wind of the sea.
s.fr: Gulliver sortit de la boîte dans le vent de la mer.

paras.summary: Men on a ship of England see the box on the waves; sailors row out with hooks and ropes, pull the box in by its great ring, answer Gulliver's calls, and cut a hole in the roof so he can come out into the wind of the sea.

s.t: The captain gave him hot food and hot drink.
s.fr: Le capitaine lui donna de la nourriture chaude et une boisson chaude.

s.t: Gulliver told the captain of the land of the giants.
s.fr: Gulliver raconta au capitaine l’histoire du pays des géants.

s.t: The captain laughed, as the other captain had laughed at the little cows.
s.fr: Le capitaine rit, comme l’autre capitaine avait ri des petites vaches.

s.t: But the sailors looked at the box, at the ring, and at the strange wood.
s.fr: Mais les marins regardèrent la boîte, la bague, et le bois étrange.

s.t: "No man of England made this box," said the captain.
s.fr: « Aucun homme d’Angleterre n’a fabriqué cette boîte, » dit-il le capitaine.

paras.summary: The captain gives Gulliver hot food and drink but laughs at his story of the giants, as the other captain once laughed at the little cows; then the sailors look at the great box with its ring and strange wood, and the captain says no man of England made it.

s.t: The ship sailed for England, week after week.
s.fr: Le navire navigua vers l’Angleterre, semaine après semaine.

s.t: At home in England, Gulliver's wife laughed and cried again to see him.
s.fr: Chez lui en Angleterre, la femme de Gulliver rit et pleura de nouveau en le voyant.

s.t: But the people of England looked strange and small to Gulliver.
s.fr: Mais les gens d’Angleterre semblaient étranges et petits à Gulliver.

s.t: He walked with great care in the town, for the men looked small as children.
s.fr: Il marchait avec grand soin dans la ville, car les hommes semblaient petits comme des enfants.

s.t: He bent his head at his own little door, for he had lived with giants.
s.fr: Il baissa la tête à sa propre petite porte, car il avait vécu avec des géants.

paras.summary: The ship sails for England, week after week, and at home Gulliver's wife laughs and cries again to see him; but for a time the people of England look strange and small, so Gulliver walks in the town with great care and bends his head at his own door.

s.t: His wife kissed him and asked him to go to sea no more.
s.fr: Sa femme l’embrassa et lui demanda de ne plus aller en mer.

s.t: Gulliver stayed home with his wife for good.
s.fr: Gulliver resta chez lui avec sa femme pour toujours.

s.t: At night, by the fire, he told his children of little Lilliput and the giants of Brobdingnag.
s.fr: Le soir, près du feu, il raconta à ses enfants le petit Lilliput et les géants de Brobdingnag.

paras.summary: His wife kisses him and asks him to go to sea no more; Gulliver stays home for good and never goes out on the great sea again, but at night, by the fire, he tells his children of little Lilliput and the giants of Brobdingnag.
